byakugan · product requirements · shipped · 2026-08-08

PRD: Markdown Pages

Agents and engineers already have Markdown lying around. Serve it as a first-class page — rendered, indexed, navigable — without letting Byakugan drift into being a static-site generator.

Problem

Byakugan only understood HTML. A docs folder in the wild is rarely that pure: READMEs, meeting notes, decision logs, and agent scratch output all arrive as .md. Those files either sat invisible next to the HTML dossier or were served as raw text — unstyled, unindexed, and outside navigation. The folder stopped being the single place to look, which is the one promise this tool makes.

Proposal

Render Markdown server-side into the same doc skeleton every other page uses, at request time, from the file on disk. One new internal package, one new dependency (goldmark: pure Go, zero transitive dependencies), and no new concepts for the reader — a Markdown page looks, searches, and navigates exactly like an HTML one.

The stylesheet ships inside the binary at /__byakugan/doc.css, so a bare folder of .md files renders fully styled with zero setup — the strongest version of the zero-config promise. Front matter is deliberately capped at three keys:

---
title: Decision log     # else: first "# heading", else: filename
status: living          # renders as a kicker badge
date: 2026-08-08
---

Requirements and status

RequirementStatus
GFM tables, strikethrough, autolinks render correctlyshipped, e2e-tested
Indexed and ranked identically to HTML pagesshipped — rendered first, then the shared extractor runs
Overlay, prev/next, live reload work unchangedshipped, e2e-tested
Works in folders with no _shared/doc.cssshipped — stylesheet served from the binary
Binary growth within budget (≤ 1.5 MB)met — one dependency, zero transitive

Out of scope — permanently

The boundary

No configuration, no templates or themes, no syntax highlighting, no table-of-contents generation, no taxonomies. Each of those is the first step toward being a worse Hugo. The moment a Markdown need exceeds this scope, the answer is: generate HTML — byakugan template exists precisely for that.

See the decision log (itself a Markdown page — this feature dogfooding itself) and the architecture overview for where the rendering sits in the pipeline.
